post_text:
Average latency is a lie that hides your worst outages.

P99s tell the truth, but even they mask the "coordinated omission" problem. 📉

Stop tracking averages; a 30-second timeout buried in 1,000 sub-millisecond requests presents as a healthy 30ms average, silencing alarms for your most frustrated users.

Account for coordinated omission where monitoring probes wait for a response before sending the next request, which artificially deflates reported latency during system saturation.

Treat throughput without error-rate segmentation as a vanity metric; high RPS on a 500-error loop is just a very efficient way to fail, yet it often triggers "healthy" scaling events in naive autoscalers. ⚙️

That part stuck with me.
lesson_extracted: Relying on averages and unsegmented throughput masks systemic failures and saturation-induced measurement bias.
